## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest)

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned
and testable independently of Dashboard releases. The format is the shared
artifact that both the Dashboard tutorial gallery (which renders and launches
tutorials) and tutorial authors (who package content per the format) build
against. It covers tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation
manifest, plus the versioning rules that let a tutorial be re-validated against
a platform release without a Dashboard release.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata structure a gallery consumer reads to display
  and launch a tutorial (title, journey, tutorial type, launch configuration).
- Define the image-pinning convention so a tutorial always runs against known
  workbench/pipeline images rather than floating tags.
- Define the validation manifest: what "tested against the current release"
  means for a tutorial, and how validation is recorded per tutorial version.
- Define tutorial versioning rules so tutorials release and validate on their
  own cadence, decoupled from Dashboard releases.
- Produce the format specification and a reference package that demonstrates
  it end to end.

Note: the format is consumed across the Dashboard, Notebooks, and Data Science
Pipelines components; the Dashboard is the primary consumer and owns the launch
contract, so the work is tracked under the Dashboard component.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written format specification exists covering metadata, pinned images, and
  the validation manifest, with no open interpretation questions for either a
  gallery implementer or a tutorial author.
- A reference tutorial package conforming to the format exists and
  demonstrates versioning and validation independent of a Dashboard release.
- A packaged tutorial's validation outcome is determinable from its validation
  manifest alone (which release it was tested against, and whether it passed).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): "A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases." Full cover. Priority raised to P0 by
  inheritance: this epic transitively enables the P0 gallery (HLR-1) and the
  P0 curated tutorials (HLR-2).

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into the user's project

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, maintained
set of tested tutorials surfaced in the console, from which a user can launch a
tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench
pre-loaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline.

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard, listing curated tutorials
  with their packaged metadata.
- Implement one-click launch for notebook-type tutorials: open a workbench in
  the user's project containing the tutorial's notebook, using the existing
  workbench creation surfaces.
- Implement one-click launch for pipeline-type tutorials: import the tutorial
  pipeline into the user's project, using the existing pipeline surfaces.
- Read tutorial packages conforming to the tutorial packaging format
  (metadata, pinned images) so launch uses the pinned images the tutorial was
  tested against.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and see the curated
  tutorials with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook-type tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project
  containing that tutorial's notebook.
- Launching a pipeline-type tutorial imports that pipeline into the user's
  project.
- End-to-end launch of at least one packaged tutorial (one notebook-type and
  one pipeline-type) succeeds against a current release build — this is the
  runtime coupling to tutorial content and is verified here as an acceptance
  gate, not a dependency on the content work.
- The gallery renders only tutorials whose validation manifest records a pass
  against the current release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook,
  or importing the pipeline)." Full cover.

# Author the notebook-based curated tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the notebook-based half of the six curated tutorials
covering the core getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first
training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is a
maintained, tested notebook packaged per the tutorial packaging format, ready
to be launched from the tutorial gallery into a workbench in the user's
project.

## Scope

- Author five tutorials that run in a workbench:
  - First workbench: creating and using a first workbench.
  - Data prep: loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  - First training run: training a first model.
  - First deployment: deploying a trained model for serving.
  - First RAG app: building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  images, and a validation manifest.
- Validate each tutorial against the current platform release and record the
  outcome in its validation manifest.
- Decide and document where the tutorial packages are hosted (existing
  notebook content repositories or another location) — an implementation
  decision for this team.

Out of scope: partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake and submission
tooling; localization of tutorial content.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials (first workbench, data prep, first training run,
  first deployment, first RAG app) exist, each packaged per the tutorial
  packaging format.
- Each tutorial's notebook runs to completion when launched into a workbench
  against the current platform release.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest records a pass against the current
  release, including the pinned images it was tested with.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys … Each
  is tested against the current release." Partial cover — the five
  notebook/workbench journeys; the first-pipeline journey is covered by the
  pipeline tutorial epic owned by the Data Science Pipelines team (different
  component and team boundary).

## Health Warnings

- This epic is a one-logical-change sweep: five notebook tutorials authored the
  same way (one packaging format, one validation path) over a surface the
  strategy presents as a single work item. It is deliberately not split.
  Estimated effort: roughly 3–5 engineer-days per tutorial (~3–4 engineer-weeks
  total). Conditional re-split trigger: if any single tutorial exceeds 5
  engineer-days of authoring/validation effort, or if hosting/validation
  infrastructure requires per-tutorial bespoke work instead of running the
  packaged validation manifests, re-split this epic into per-tutorial (or
  per-journey-group) epics.

# Document tutorial gallery usage and the tutorial contribution process

## Description

This epic authors the product documentation for the tutorial gallery: how
users find and launch tutorials from the gallery, and how teams contribute new
tutorials. It is authored after the gallery and the curated tutorials exist so
the documentation describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to be authored):

- Using the tutorial gallery: finding tutorials, understanding what each
  journey covers, launching a tutorial into your project (workbench with the
  notebook, or imported pipeline), and what happens in your project after
  launch.
- Contributing new tutorials: the contribution process, how a tutorial is
  packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest), and how validation against the current release is
  recorded.
- Explicitly out of scope per the strategy: submission tooling for partner or
  community contributions is not documented as a feature this release (the
  process is documented; no tooling exists).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the gallery to find and launch
  tutorials into a project.
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials,
  including packaging and validation requirements.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and the shipped curated tutorials (screenshots and steps match the actual
  behavior).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): "Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials." Full cover.
